options.text: The same pass rate, only cheaper.
options.why: Tempting. A cost saving on a change that cuts turns is not a free one.

options.text: A lower pass rate: the change cut runs that need more turns.
options.why: Right. The held-out tasks script more replies than four turns allow.

options.text: Nothing changes: the tasks are the same.
options.why: Tempting. The tasks are the same; the harness is not.

outcome: On the scripted board the held-out tasks pass 0 of 10 after the change, against 10 of 10 before, and the cost fell. The change did not do what it was for.
question: You set the turn limit to four and the cost falls on every task. What do you expect on the held-out tasks?

options.text: That the step's transcript matches the expected output, in a temp folder.
options.why: Right. The checkpoint is the expected transcript, and the test runs it.

options.text: That the code has no bugs.
options.why: Tempting and wrong. A checkpoint shows one run, not the absence of bugs.

options.text: That the steps pass in the browser only.
options.why: Tempting and wrong. The same check runs under CPython and Pyodide.

question: A checkpoint becomes a test. What does the test check?

options.text: The spend: a request that could pass the cap is not sent.
options.why: Right. The cap is checked before each request, and the run stops with status budget.

options.text: The model's answers, so they stay short.
options.why: Tempting and wrong. The cap limits money, not length.

options.text: The key, so it is never printed.
options.why: Tempting and wrong. The key rule is separate; the cap is about spend.

question: What does --max-cost-usd protect on a live run?

options.text: A baseline: the same tasks and seeds, without the change.
options.why: Right. Then the difference is the change and nothing else.

options.text: The author's memory of the last run.
options.why: Tempting and wrong. Memory is not a measurement.

options.text: The best of all the trials.
options.why: Tempting and wrong. Picking the best trial hides the rest.

question: A change is measured against what?
